dataset.description:
During the project, several categories of data will be collected:
1. Personal information: age, gender, nationality, ethnicity (cultural characteristics), and race (physical characteristics).
2. Anthropometric measurements: height (m), weight (kg), waist circumference (cm), hip circumference (cm), neck circumference (cm), blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), and heart rate (beats/min).
3. Medical history: type and duration of diabetes mellitus (DM), diabetic complications, diabetic nephropathy, dialysis status, history of kidney transplantation, other kidney diseases, and relevant comorbidities.
4. Medications: insulin, other antidiabetic agents, blood pressure medications, cholesterol-lowering medications, and other therapies.
5. Socio-economic status: education level, occupation, and current employment/living situation.
6. Lifestyle factors: smoking status and alcohol consumption.
7. Laboratory analyses: glucose, HbA1c, cholesterol, triglycerides, creatinine, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio.
8. Biomarkers: obtained from biopsy samples, serum, fecal samples, and urine examinations.
9. Gastrointestinal symptoms: assessed using standardized questionnaires.
All data will be compiled into a summary of results in tabular form and included in the statistical dataset.

distribution.title: This will be the first study to investigate the association between the biomarkers of intestinal permeability in different biological material (intestinal biopsies, faeces, serum), DKD progression rate and early biomarkers of DKD in T1D. By performing intestinal biopsies in all the included subjects, we will be able to assess associations between intestinal integrity and inflammation markers, serum intestinal permeability markers, and early DKD biomarkers.

dataset.title: Clinical data for gut-kidney axis in type 1 diabetes patients

dmp.description: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disease characterized by insulin deficiency and hyperglycaemia, as well as the development of late complications, including nephropathy. Pathogenetic mechanisms have not been fully investigated in the case of progressive diabetic nephropathy. Our hypotheses are that intestinal inflammation and permeability could be one of the factors contributing to glucose variability, systemic inflammation and thus - the progression of diabetic nephropathy. Within the framework of this project, type 1 diabetes patients with progressive nephropathy and stable kidney disease will be selected from the longitudinal study LatDiane, which was founded in 2013. In the biological samples of the patients, faecal inflammatory markers, as well as markers of inflammation and markers of bacterial translocation in the blood will be studied. To assess the relationship between intestinal inflammation and permeability, endoscopic examinations with histological and immunohistochemical analysis of biopsy material will be performed in patients with gastrointestinal symptoms. The project will result in data that may help in the future to treat the progression of diabetic nephropathy by influencing intestinal inflammation and systemic responses.
